title: Mitigate intermittent tenant hostname shadowing during dedicated VPC peering resync
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several Dedicated customers reported that after scheduled capacity resizes and VPC peering reconverges, internal tenant hostnames were intermittently resolved to other tenants' endpoints (hostname shadowing). This resulted in misrouted traffic, failed TLS handshakes, and a small number of customer-facing errors. The issue is intermittent and correlates with peering reconnect + SNAT table churn during scale operations.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create two Dedicated tenants (A and B) with peering between customer VPCs
2) Deploy services in both tenants that expose private hostnames (internal-service.customer.local)
3) Trigger an autoscaler-driven GPU pool resize that causes peering reconnection and SNAT pool reallocation
4) Observe DNS responses from tenant resolvers for internal hostnames during reconverge window; some queries return endpoints belonging to other tenant
5) Reproduce is flaky; requires concurrent resolver cache entries and ephemeral SNAT port reuse during connection rebinds
root_cause: Race between VPC peering route reprogramming and egress SNAT port reuse combined with delayed resolver cache invalidation. When peering endpoints were reparented, some dataplane nodes continued replying to DNS queries with stale local resolver bindings while SNAT translations had already been reallocated, producing cross-tenant association windows.
mitigation_taken: Applied a short-lived control-plane throttling rule to serialize peering reparent operations for affected Dedicated GPU pools; increased resolver cache expiry and added conservative SNAT ephemeral port partitioning to tenant-specific ranges as an immediate mitigation to reduce cross-tenant reuse.
fix_summary: Long-term fix involves two parts: (1) ensure route reprogramming is atomic w.r.t. resolver cache invalidation by adding a 'peer-reparent barrier' in the control plane so nodes flush resolver caches only after routes and vNI mapping are fully committed; (2) implement deterministic SNAT ephemeral range allocation per-tenant on scale-down to prevent ephemeral port collisions during rebind. Changes implemented in controlplane/vpc-manager and dataplane/egress-nat modules.
canary_and_rollout_plan: 1) Canary 5% of Dedicated clusters in staging region with peer-reparent barrier enabled
2) Validate resolver cache flush timing and absence of cross-tenant DNS answers for 24 hours
3) Enable deterministic SNAT range allocation for canary clusters
4) Gradually ramp to 100% over 48 hours with monitoring gates
5) If elevated error rates observed, rollback SNAT change independently while keeping barrier enabled
monitoring_and_checks: Add a tenant-isolation SLI that tracks any DNS answer where the returned endpoint IP maps to a different tenant (existing mapping telemetry)
Create Grafana dashboard: 'peering-reparentness -> cross-tenant-dns' with alert threshold 0.01% queries
Post-deploy noise check: verify TLS handshake error rate for affected tenants remains within baseline +/- 5%
Synthetic checker: periodic internal lookup for representative hostnames across tenants and assert no cross-tenant IPs
postmortem_notes: Root cause was an interplay of control-plane ordering and dataplane resource reuse. We under-estimated the window of possible stale resolver state during vNI/route transition. The 'peer-reparent barrier' approach adds a small additional delay to peering ops but eliminates the inconsistent state window. Deterministic SNAT partitioning reduces blast radius during ephemeral port rebinds.
